Repository implementation guide. Snapshot: 12 October 2026.

## Durable records
The manual-organization ledger is atomically written through a temporary file, file fsync, rename and directory fsync. Manual edits persist a prepared transaction before publication. Startup recovery replays recorded decisions, filtering links whose endpoint versions changed, then removes the prepared transaction marker.

| Interruption point | Recovery principle |
| --- | --- |
| Before a prepared ledger exists | Existing published organization remains authoritative. |
| After preparation before all index rows publish | Startup rolls the recorded decisions forward. |
| Ordinary publication failure | The edit path can restore the earlier ledger/rows. |
| During grouping reset clearing | Replay uncheckpointed clears before rebuilding. |
| During filter publication | Reconcile chunk filters from document metadata. |

## Candidate preparation strategy
Topic preparation uses sparse hashed features rather than a document-by-vocabulary dense matrix or unrestricted pairwise hierarchical clustering. The fixed feature budget is 8,192 and the topic/centroid budget is 128. Cluster naming samples at most twenty-four texts. Large buckets use bounded minibatch centroids; smaller buckets use sparse online assignment.

## Scope first
ProjectNames provides exact-name lookup. Shared vocabulary combines explicit paths, ordinary-prose subjects and suitable existing folder names. Rank candidates inside the recognized project scope. Unknown scope is not permission to choose another company's folder. Existing stored vectors can rank a bounded set of scoped prototypes without reembedding every original.

## Explicit selection
The human bulk-download route accepts 1–100 explicitly selected document/version pairs and caps total content at one GiB. It first validates the complete selection. A missing version stops the action with affected IDs instead of silently producing an incomplete success archive.

## Original bytes
Each entry comes from storage.read_file for the pinned version, including its size/hash verification. The ZIP uses stored entries and a disk-backed temporary archive. It is delivered as a file response and cleaned after delivery; browser handling creates a bounded Blob and revokes its object URL.

Uploaded names are reduced to basenames, controls are removed and special empty/dot names receive a safe replacement. Case-insensitive collisions gain numeric suffixes before their extension. These rules protect ZIP entry paths while retaining exact content bytes.

Folder overview and Document map change presentation, not retrieval or Jev evaluation. Folder frames contain immediate-child documents. title: Symbiknow / Architecture / Concurrency and safe publication | text: # Symbiknow / Architecture / Concurrency and safe publication

Repository implementation guide. Snapshot: 12 October 2026.
## One owner per library
The application takes a process owner lock for its configured data directory. Browser requests and HTTP MCP clients share the same lifecycle and ingestion worker. A separate stdio server must not be started against a data directory already owned by the web server.

## Locks and model work
server.write_lock serializes lifecycle mutations and INDEX_LOCK protects index operations. Native storage has its own write locking. The embedding adapter caches one runtime and serializes inference. A model response is never sufficient permission to publish obsolete content: source and related target versions must remain current.

## Races that matter
An upload can advance the head while older indexing or Jev work is running. Current retrieval rejects the old version independently through both index metadata and OCFL head checks. An in-flight ordinary organization decision cannot overwrite a manual folder correction or a document captured by an active rebuild. Deletion must not be undone by an old indexing result or replayed upload receipt.

## The stale-hit problem
Suppose v1 is indexed and v2 has committed while reindexing is pending. A vector/full-text engine may still contain v1 rows. Current search must not label those as evidence for v2 merely because the document ID matches.

## Layered gates
find_documents starts with active chunks and optional organization/model filters. For each hit it verifies the documents row is indexed, that indexed_version and version match the chunk version, and that the independently read OCFL current head agrees. Missing/deleted heads are rejected.

The public MCP search then checks heads again before returning matches. It performs another check after optional hosted Jev evaluation, since a content update can occur while the provider is answering. Stored links are also checked against target versions.

title: Symbiknow / Architecture / Data ownership and system flow | text: # Symbiknow / Architecture / Data ownership and system flow

Repository implementation guide. Snapshot: 12 October 2026.
## What owns the data
Symbiknow is one Python application with a shared human interface and MCP endpoint. Original bytes and per-version metadata belong to the OCFL repository managed through rocfl. LanceDB documents, chunks, vectors and organization are derived representations. React owns presentation state, including selection and saved canvas geometry; it is not the owner of original documents.

## Upload-to-answer flow
1. An MCP or browser upload sends actual bytes to the existing server.
2. Storage commits an OCFL version, then the server registers its current head and schedules ingestion.
3. One worker converts the committed original, chunks text, computes local embeddings and publishes current-version index rows.
4. Jev can choose folder/group metadata and version-pinned links using supplied textual evidence.
5. Retrieval returns current-version evidence; optional answerability adds judgments over that evidence.
6. Download reads the pinned original from OCFL and reports its SHA-256.

There is no second graph database or fallback embedding runtime. Backups and recovery must distinguish irreplaceable originals from reconstructable indexes and durable operational receipts.

## Independent outcomes
An upload's stored result confirms committed bytes. Searchability requires an indexed current version. Organization is a further step with its own status. These outcomes should never be collapsed into one success badge.

| --- | --- |
| pending | Original stored; current content awaits indexing. |

| empty | No textual or visual evidence was extracted. |

The worker reads a committed version and verifies its hash before conversion. Text embeddings are computed in small batches; visual embeddings are processed individually. ## Request shape
A download item identifies document_id and optionally version, offset, length and history. Range length must be positive and within the configured chunk limit. ## Supported content
The indexing predicate accepts plain text, Markdown, HTML/XHTML, PDF and common image types including PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF, with corresponding recognized extensions. Unsupported originals remain stored and downloadable.

## Text structure
Docling conversion preserves document structure. HybridChunker uses the embedding tokenizer and a 512-token chunking bound unless a supplied test tokenizer replaces it. Extracted evidence includes contextualized text and structural/page provenance. Plain-text content is wrapped into a Docling document before chunking.

## Visual content
PDF conversion requests page images and textual extraction. Native images preserve visual representations independently from available OCR text. Multi-frame image inputs are indexed by frame while their compressed original remains intact. An OCR failure for an image can leave its native visual representation searchable.

## Different representation bases
Native visual chunks have a vector and page/frame provenance but no textual answer passage. OCR/text chunks have actual extracted text and provenance. An image can have both forms, or remain visually searchable when OCR fails.

## Retrieval and judgment
Semantic retrieval can return visually related content without a text quotation. The UI distinguishes Visual match / Not checked. Jev's textual answerability input filters out native visual-only rows; textless candidates cannot establish a direct or partial answer.

An OCR-derived answer may be checked over its text while disclosing OCR evidence. That does not guarantee perfect transcription, entity recognition or page-wide understanding. The evidence ID and original version remain the reproducibility boundary.
